nutshell: Unsupervised clothing-change person ReID (UCC-ReID) relies on clustering to generate pseudo-labels, but clustering algorithms often fail to group images of the same person wearing different clothes into the same cluster ('unconnected positive pairs'), which hinders clothing-invariant learning. ICSM addresses this with a three-stage pipeline: cluster images using all available signal (including clothing) to get compact clusters, represent each cluster's identity and clothing as learned CLIP text-prompt embeddings, then use inter-cluster similarity to link clusters of the same person across clothing changes and optimize only over reliable pairs.
contributions: A three-stage framework (clothing-aware clustering -> cluster-level CLIP-based identity/clothing text features -> inter-cluster similarity estimation) that connects clothing-change positive pairs at the cluster level rather than trying to match instances directly.

Inter-cluster similarity estimation (ISE, Eq. 8-10): ranks all other clusters by cluster-level identity-feature and clothing-feature similarity to define, for each cluster, a clothing-change-positive set, a reliable-negative set, and a hard-negative set, then restricts the contrastive/classification losses (Eq. 11-12) to only these reliable sets instead of optimizing indiscriminately over all pairs.

Two additional text-semantic contrastive losses (identity-oriented Lis, clothing-invariant Lcs) that align an image's similarity distribution over cluster centroids with the corresponding distribution over cluster-level CLIP text-prompt embeddings, injecting extra supervision beyond the clustering signal.

New state-of-the-art among unsupervised CC-ReID methods across 5 datasets (PRCC, VC-Clothes, LTCC, Celeb-reID, Celeb-reID-light) and competitive with several supervised CC-ReID methods, with training time close to prior unsupervised methods despite the extra stages (Table 3).
deficiencies: The paper's own ablation (Table 4) shows ISE alone (M2) already captures most of the total improvement over the baseline (e.g. PRCC(CC) mAP: 43.9 -> 53.6 out of an eventual 57.8, roughly 73% of the total gain), while the two text-semantic losses (Lis, Lcs) that the abstract/intro foreground as a key contribution ('leverages text semantics') each add comparatively modest increments (M2->M3 +3.2, M2->M4 +1.7 mAP) - the clustering/ISE structure appears to do most of the actual work.

The critical ISE rank-percentile hyperparameters (γa=2%, γc=50%, γb=60%) are only sensitivity-tested on PRCC(CC) and VC-Clothes(CC) (Fig. 7-8); generalization to LTCC, Celeb-reID, and Celeb-reID-light - datasets with very different identity counts and gallery sizes - is never verified.

Stage I's DBSCAN pseudo-labels are frozen and reused unchanged for stages II and III with no further re-clustering (stated explicitly in Sec. 4.2), so any clustering errors in the initial 'compact clusters' propagate uncorrected through the rest of the pipeline; this risk is never discussed or measured.

Absolute performance on Celeb-reID/Celeb-reID-light (mAP 7.0/7.7) is drastically lower than on PRCC/VC-Clothes (mAP 57.8/73.5), and the paper never investigates why - Celeb-reID has few or single images per outfit per identity, which plausibly breaks the compact-cluster assumption the whole method depends on, but this isn't analyzed.
notable: The 'cluster-level identity feature' and 'cluster-level clothing feature' are not pooled image features at all - they are the optimized embeddings of learnable CLIP text prompts ('a photo of a [S1]...[SM] person' / 'a photo of [C1]...[CM] clothing'), so the entire cross-cluster matching signal in stage III runs through a frozen CLIP text encoder used as a per-cluster embedding lookup rather than through visual features directly. This is a more central use of CLIP-ReID-style prompt learning than typical auxiliary-loss usage, and could be a reusable pattern for other cluster-linking problems beyond ReID.
